transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-05-19 15:30 UTC
- Duration: ~62 minutes
- Attendees: Jared (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Miguel (Redwood SE), Alex (VectorEdge NetOps), Samira (Platform), Evan (CTO), Tanya (Security)

Summary (auto): 72h telemetry review; discuss spike mitigation; kernel upgrade plan; MTU testing; next steps and owners.

Topics: perf, routing fallback, kernel canary, MTU, KMS/logs, dedicated sizing spreadsheet.

Transcript:
00:00 Jared: ok everyone, thanks for hopping on for the weekly pilot sync, I know we've got a full agenda, we'll start with the 72 hour showback.
00:18 Alex: yeah thanks, uh quick note, we pulled the flow logs and I think the spike was around 03:14 UTC on the 14th, lots of retransmits, looked like the egress paths got congested.
00:34 Priya: ok can you confirm that was through the direct peering or the backup egress? because our fallback routing would have switched routes there.
00:45 Alex: um I think it was the backup, the primary peering hit a transient flurry, so traffic shifted to the fallback route and that route had a higher MTU mismatch, possibly causing fragmentation and retransmits.
01:02 Miguel: mhm, that matches the telemetry, we saw p50 at 42ms but p95 jumped to 410ms for a short window, and a small tail at p99 set off the circuit breaker.
01:18 Evan: when you say circuit breaker, is that the redwood side automatic fallback or our load balancer kicking things?
01:26 Priya: good question, so we have two layers — our client-side routing policy and then the platform-level fallback. On the incident we saw platform fallback engage after repeated egress errors, the request was routed to a lower-capacity variant which increased latency.
01:45 Alex: one thing I noticed, the VPC had MTU at 1500, but the onprem switch had jumbo frames allowed — there may be mismatched MTU which caused fragments to be dropped.
01:58 Samira: right, we haven't tested jumbo frames in staging, we can toggle MTU but we worry about blackholing traffic.
02:12 Jared: ok let's table MTU test as an action, Samira will enable MTU 9000 on a single rack in staging and we'll watch for failures.
02:22 Samira: yes will do.
02:29 Priya: regarding the kernel upgrade — we've seen modest perf improvements on our internal runs but it's not universal. The canary will show if the newer kernel affects the serving runtime's collectors or the NIC offload behaviour.
02:47 Evan: are there specific kernel patches? I want to avoid regressing on NIC drivers.
02:54 Priya: it's mostly netstack and some scheduled nic driver updates, and the newer kernel seems to handle large receive offload a bit differently; that can affect small-payload latencies.
03:10 Miguel: also we should mention KV cache warmup — in the synthetic bursts we saw a 30% improvement in average token latency when cache was primed, so the dedicated sizing should account for warmup profile.
03:28 Alex: for the May 14 spike I'll upload pcap and VPC flow logs to the shared drive, is that the folder under /shared/pilot-telemetry?
03:36 Jared: yes that's the one, I'll send the link after the call.
03:43 Tanya: on the security front, quick question: are pilot logs encrypted with customer KMS or Redwood-managed keys? we need to add that to our compliance questionnaire.
03:53 Jared: good call — by default logs are encrypted with Redwood-managed keys but for Private we can integrate with customer KMS; Tanya, can you confirm the scope you need?
04:05 Tanya: we need proof that key material never leaves our HSM and that audit logs are immutable for 90 days.
04:13 Jared: ok we'll produce the integration note and update the SAML/SOC2 docs, I'll push that to the shared security artefacts.
04:21 Evan: circling back to fallback thresholds, what metric exactly triggers the platform fallback — error pct, latency, or both?
04:29 Priya: right now it's primarily error percentage on the egress path plus sustained tail latency beyond a configured window. Our suggestion: bump error threshold from 5% to 8% for this workload and run a staged simulation.
04:45 Miguel: simulation plan would be: inject 5-10% synthetic packet loss on the staging fallback route and watch routing decisions, plus ensure no cascading rollbacks.
04:58 Alex: that simulation would be very helpful, please include step-by-step so our infra team can mirror it.
05:08 Priya: we'll document runbook steps and include the exact sysctl and kernel args we changed in our internal canary.
05:16 Jared: ok next topic, dedicated sizing — we ran the 5k qps baseline but haven't done the 10k burst with warm cache, can we schedule that?
05:26 Evan: we want the 10k burst to see tail behaviour, especially at p99. Also include a run with quantized weights vs fp16 to compare throughput.
05:35 Miguel: note — quantized run will reduce GPU memory pressure but might slightly vary latency distribution, we'll annotate that in the sheet.
05:46 Samira: any blockers for kernel canary? we need a maintenance window.
05:52 Priya: we only need a short window (20 minutes) on two staging nodes; low risk but we will monitor NIC metrics closely.
06:00 Alex: I'll gather the pcap and flow logs and drop them in the folder.
06:07 Tanya: I'll confirm KMS policy and send the compliance note.
06:12 Jared: great. quick check — competitors mentioned? we get asked about self-hosting or another vendor, but for now the main ask is control over keys and predictable latency.
06:25 Evan: ok let's set the next sync to Friday morning to review canary results and the 10k run.
06:33 Jared: works for Redwood, we'll book it. I'll also share the dedicated sizing worksheet and pricing showback after the call.
06:40 Miguel: i'll put the simulation steps and the fallback threshold proposal into the runbook doc.
06:47 Priya: action recap: kernel canary (Priya), MTU staging test (Samira), packet captures (Alex), KMS confirmation (Tanya), pricing sheet (Jared).
06:58 Jared: perfect, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in writing and post artifacts.
07:02 [call ends]

Artifacts mentioned:

- dedicated sizing worksheet: https://redwood.cloud/worksheets/dedicated-sizing-ve-2026-0043.xlsx
